text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended Wednesday.

LONDON - British shares dropped, reversing Tuesday's gains as a second day of declines on Wall Street took the steam out of bourses across Europe. The FTSE 100 index closed down 16.3 points at 4,045.2.

FRANKFURT - German blue-chip shares, coming off an all-time high reached on Tuesday, closed down 0.72 percent as some investors turned to profit-taking in a quiet bourse trading session. The DAX index, which reached a record close of 2,886.98 points Tuesday, fell 20.91 points to end at 2,866.07 points. Later the IBIS DAX, which measures all-day computer trade in the DAX index stood at 2,880.89 down 19.87 points.

PARIS - CAC 40 stocks closed with losses except Eurotunnel, which showed a gain, and Cie Generale des Eaux, which was unchanged. Traders said the market needed to take profits before resuming its advance with the goal of regaining the historic high of 2,360.98 points set in 1994. The CAC 40 closed down 40.46 points at 2308.65.

ZURICH - Swiss shares closed lower after Tuesday's record run amid insecurity about near-term developments on Wall Street. The Blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) lost 13.9 points, or 0.35 percent, to end at 3,910.6. The All-share SPI was down 8.85 points to 2,495.61.

TOKYO - Tokyo stocks ended mixed in directionless trade with the key Nikkei edging up slightly. After an initial dip at the open on Wall Street's losses, buying was limited to selected blue-chip issues, while the recent fall in other issues lost momentum. The key Nikkei 225 average inched up 29.35 points or 0.14 percent to finish at 20,659.91.

HONG KONG - Cautious market sentiment drove Hong Kong stocks to a weaker close, but bargain-hunting allowed prices to finish off their lows. The Hang Seng index closed with a loss of 22.02 points at 13,434.24.

SYDNEY - An active Australian stock market slid to a lower close as the market followed the Dow down early and quickly settling in about 10 points lower. By the close, the All Ordinaries index lost 9.4 points to stand at 2,370.7.

JOHANNESBURG - A scramble for South African gold shares ensued during the afternoon as the bullion price rose from three-year lows touched on Tuesday and as the rand weakened almost one cent. There was strong local and foreign interest in gold stocks. The gold index added 1.6 percent or 24.1 points to 1,516.5. Industrial shares ended weak for the third consecutive day amid a general lack of direction and a softer rand which ended the day at 4.66 against the dollar. The Industrial index fell 23.1 points to 7,968.6. The overall market index was 14.1 points firmer at 6,713.6.
